title: The specified finite comparison is an isomorphism of complexes
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes, and let $n\geq0$ index the positive exponent $n+1$. For every unbounded cochain complex $K$ of sheaves of modules over the finite constant coefficient ring $(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1})_Y$, the specified tensor-unit chain map $\kappa_K:GK\to g^*K$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] is an isomorphism of complexes. Here $G$ is the sectionwise inverse image with action transported through the inverse of the canonical coefficient-ring comparison, as in [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. The site universe and coefficient universe are independent. No boundedness, constructibility, flatness or completeness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Step 3 of lem-weil-point-automorphism-derived-transport-inverse: the finite scalar-extension isomorphism and identification of its inverse with the specified comparison. Stacks 03D2, 03D6 and 00WX.

proof.text: Let F be postcomposition by g and G the pro-etale base-change functor, with their map/pullback adjunction. For the finite constant ring, write psi for the canonical direct ring map and c for inverseImageFiniteCoefficientMap. The adjunct F*(psi) followed by the sheaf adjunction counit agrees with c: after precomposing with constant presheaf sections this is the defining sheafification hom-equivalence equation and naturality of toSheafify along proEtaleIsoCommaArrow. Uniqueness of isoSectionwiseConstantMap gives the equality. Hence psi is the adjoint of c.

source.place: Step 3 of lem-weil-point-automorphism-derived-transport-inverse: the finite scalar-extension isomorphism and identification of its inverse with the specified comparison. Stacks 03D2, 03D6 and 00WX.

proof.text: Transport actions through the inverse of c. The two coefficient compatibility equations for SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardAdj follow from the preceding adjunct equation, inverse identities for c, and the sheaf adjunction triangle identity. That Mathlib construction supplies an adjunction from inverseImageFiniteModules to coefficientProEtaleModuleDirectImage. Its counit on sections is restriction along the site adjunction unit, namely proEtaleIsoCommaArrow.

source.place: Step 3 of lem-weil-point-automorphism-derived-transport-inverse: the finite scalar-extension isomorphism and identification of its inverse with the specified comparison. Stacks 03D2, 03D6 and 00WX.

proof.text: The recorded finite pullback is another left adjoint of exactly that module direct image. Apply Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq to get a natural isomorphism from sectionwise inverse image to pullback. Its component is the image of the pullback adjunction unit followed by the sectionwise adjunction counit, by homEquiv_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app. On sections this is the pullback generator restricted along proEtaleIsoCommaArrow, exactly the normalization in inverseImageFiniteComparison_existsUnique. Uniqueness identifies the recorded chain map with this natural isomorphism mapped to complexes, which is invertible.

theorem inverseImageFiniteComparisonComplex_isIso
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t}} (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g] (n : ℕ)
    (K : CochainComplex (integralOperationsFiniteModules l E Y n) ℤ) :
    IsIso (inverseImageFiniteComparisonComplex l E g n K)
